consequence.statement: Logs RBAC is enforced by default; the logs tab on pod view is not visible to users/groups/roles without explicit `logs, get` permission.
consequence.remediation: Grant explicit `logs, get` permissions to the users/groups/roles that need log access; remove server.rbac.log.enforce.enable from argocd-cm after upgrade.

original.statement: Starting in 3.0 the argocd-cm flag server.rbac.log.enforce.enable is removed and logs RBAC is always enforced, so the logs tab on pod view is hidden unless users have explicit `logs, get` permission.

consequence.statement: Users, groups and roles that relied on `applications, get` for implicit logs access lose it. The `logs` tab on pod view is not visible to them unless they are granted explicit `logs, get` permission.
consequence.remediation: Grant explicit `logs, get` permissions to the users/groups/roles that need log access. After the upgrade, remove server.rbac.log.enforce.enable from argocd-cm if it was set.

corrected.statement: In Argo CD 3.0 the argocd-cm flag server.rbac.log.enforce.enable is removed and logs RBAC is enforced by default. Users who only had logs access implicitly through `applications, get` lose it: the `logs` tab on pod view is not visible without explicit `logs, get` permission.

decision.reason: [ev-19231a7aa629] says that in 2.3 and earlier, users with `applications, get` automatically got logs access. From 3.0 the enforcement flag is removed and logs RBAC is enforced by default, so the `logs` tab will not be visible without explicit `logs, get`. The section is listed under Breaking Changes and tells affected users to perform remediation steps. Users losing access they had before is permission-lost, not a behavior change that keeps working, so the class becomes action-required.
